You are auditing the frontend of a Tauri v2 desktop voice-transcription app at /Users/egortokarev/Code/voxfusion/packages/app (the src/ directory — TypeScript/TSX, Tailwind). First determine whether it's React or SolidJS (check package.json, vite.config.ts, index.tsx) — the README claims SolidJS.

Your job: find every meaningful improvement opportunity in the frontend code. Read ALL files under packages/app/src/ (it's ~8k lines; read them fully, not just excerpts). Look for:

1. **Correctness bugs**: race conditions, stale closures/reactivity mistakes, unhandled promise rejections, event-listener leaks (especially Tauri `listen()` cleanup), incorrect effect dependencies or Solid reactivity misuse, error paths that swallow failures.
2. **Refactoring**: duplicated logic across pages (Dictionary*/Style* pages look like near-clones — quantify the duplication), god components, dead code, inconsistent patterns for calling Tauri commands, missing shared abstractions.
3. **Performance**: unnecessary re-renders/recomputation, unbounded lists (TranscriptionList), missing virtualization/pagination, polling where events would do, heavy work on every keystroke, favicon fetching behavior.
4. **UX in code**: missing loading/error/empty states, missing optimistic updates, missing keyboard accessibility (focus traps in modals, Escape handling), missing aria labels, hardcoded English strings that bypass the i18n system (grep for user-visible string literals in TSX), i18n keys present in en.ts but missing in other locales (compare key sets across translations/*.ts programmatically with a script).
5. **State/store issues**: settingsStore.ts design, localStorage vs backend persistence inconsistencies.

For EVERY finding give: `file:line`, one-sentence problem statement, one-sentence concrete fix, and a severity (high/medium/low). Order by severity. Be exhaustive but concrete — no generic advice like "add tests". Verify each claim against the actual code before including it (quote the offending line). Your final message is the deliverable: a markdown findings list, nothing else.

- agent-browser: Browser automation CLI for AI agents. Use when the user needs to interact with websites, including navigating pages, filling forms, clicking buttons, taking screenshots, extracting data, testing web apps, or automating any browser task. Triggers include requests to "open a website", "fill out a form", "click a button", "take a screenshot", "scrape data from a page", "test this web app", "login to a site", "automate browser actions", or any task requiring programmatic web interaction. Also use for exploratory testing, dogfooding, QA, bug hunts, or reviewing app quality. Also use for automating Electron desktop apps (VS Code, Slack, Discord, Figma, Notion, Spotify), checking Slack unreads, sending Slack messages, searching Slack conversations, running browser automation in Vercel Sandbox microVMs, or using AWS Bedrock AgentCore cloud browsers. Prefer agent-browser over any built-in browser automation or web tools.
- portless: Set up and use portless for named local dev server URLs (e.g. https://myapp.localhost instead of http://localhost:3000). Use when integrating portless into a project, configuring dev server names, setting up the local proxy, working with .localhost domains, or troubleshooting port/proxy issues.
- codecast: Get codecast dashboard and share links for current session (user)
- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- frontend-design:frontend-design: Guidance for distinctive, intentional visual design when building new UI or reshaping an existing one. Helps with aesthetic direction, typography, and making choices that don't read as templated defaults.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

All files under `packages/app/src/` have been read in full (~9,000 lines). Framework verdict first, then findings.

---

# VoxFusion Frontend Audit — `/Users/egortokarev/Code/voxfusion/packages/app/src`

**Framework: SolidJS** (confirmed via `package.json` deps `solid-js`/`vite-plugin-solid`/`@solidjs/router`, `vite.config.ts` `plugins: [solid()]`, and `render()` from `solid-js/web` in `index.tsx`). The README claim is correct — but several bugs below are React idioms that silently do nothing in Solid.

All paths below are under `/Users/egortokarev/Code/voxfusion/packages/app/` (line numbers refer to the files there).

---

## HIGH

1. **`src/pages/VoiceControl.tsx:100,309` — the overlay window transcribes with the wrong style: `settings()` is never initialized in this window.** `initSettings()` is only called in `src/App.tsx:94` (main window); the voice-control window is a separate JS context, so `useSettings()` returns `DEFAULT_SETTINGS` forever, and `transcribeAudio(..., settings().defaultStyle)` always passes `"default"`, ignoring the user's configured default style (line 322 also logs the wrong style). Fix: keep a local `defaultStyle` signal fed from `loadSettings()` in `onMount` and refreshed in the existing `settings-changed` listener (which already updates mic/mute but forgot style).

2. **`src/components/SettingsModal.tsx:81-92` — React-ism: `createEffect` "returns a cleanup function", which Solid treats as an accumulator value, never a cleanup.** `return () => window.removeEventListener("keydown", handleEscape)` never runs, so every modal open adds another permanent window `keydown` listener (and Escape keeps firing `onClose` even when the modal is closed). Fix: `onCleanup(() => window.removeEventListener(...))` inside the effect.

3. **`src/components/settings/ModelSettings.tsx:35-46` — `onCleanup` registered after `await` inside an async `onMount` runs outside the reactive owner and never executes**, so the `"model-download-progress"` listener leaks every time the Model section is opened (the component is unmounted/remounted by the `<Show>` in `SettingsModal.tsx:139`). Each leaked handler keeps mutating a disposed component's signals and calling `refresh()`. Fix: register a synchronous `onCleanup` with an `unlisten` variable + `disposed` flag (the correct pattern already exists in `UpdateNotification.tsx:64-80`).

4. **`src/components/onboarding/steps/ModelDownloadStep.tsx:33-41` — same bug family: `onCleanup(() => unlisten())` after two `await`s is a no-op**, leaking a `"model-download-progress"` listener each time step 5 mounts (navigating Back/Next in the wizard remounts it). Same fix as #3.

5. **`src/components/UpdateNotification.tsx:104,152 — update progress bar is mathematically meaningless.** `const progress = downloadProgress() + event.data.chunkLength;` accumulates raw **bytes** into the signal, and the bar renders `width: ${Math.min(downloadProgress() / 10, 100)}%` — i.e. full after 1,000 bytes; `event.data.contentLength` (line 95) is checked but never stored, and `downloadedBytes` (line 91) duplicates the signal. Fix: capture `contentLength` on `Started` and set `progress = downloadedBytes / contentLength * 100`.

## MEDIUM — correctness

6. **`src/components/onboarding/OnboardingWizard.tsx:32-57` — double-click on Next/Back skips steps.** `goToNext` has no `isAnimating()` guard; two clicks inside the 200 ms `setTimeout` window each compute `currentStep() + 1` at fire time, advancing two steps and bypassing the next step's `canProceed()` gating (permission/download checks). Fix: `if (isAnimating()) return;` at the top of both.

7. **`src/pages/VoiceControl.tsx:207-250` — concurrent hotkey re-registration race.** The `settings-changed` and `learning-step-active` handlers both `await registerShortcuts(...)`; `registerDictationHotkeys` (`src/lib/hotkeyUtils.ts:309-331`) has no mutex — if call A is mid-registration when call B runs `unregisterDictationHotkey()` (a no-op, since A hasn't assigned `registeredDictationHotkeys` yet), A's registrations get overwritten by B's assignment and leak, so one key press fires two handlers (start+stop instantly). Fix: serialize registration through a promise chain/mutex in `hotkeyUtils.ts`.

8. **`src/components/TranscriptionList.tsx:100-103,129-132` — `unlisten` assigned after `await listen(...)`; unmounting before the promise resolves leaks the `"transcription-created"` listener**, which then calls `fetchTranscriptions()` into a disposed component forever. Same race in `src/components/onboarding/steps/AccessibilityPermissionStep.tsx:80-82` (`unlistenFn` set after `await`). Fix: `disposed` flag checked in the `.then`, as in `UpdateNotification.tsx`.

9. **`src/App.tsx:139,148,154,164` — four `onCleanup` calls after `await`s in async `onMount` are no-ops** (owner lost; Solid logs "cleanups created outside a root will never be run"). Harmless today only because `App` never unmounts, but it breaks HMR in dev and is a trap for copy-paste (see #3/#4 where the same pattern already bit). Fix: hoist unlisten vars and one synchronous `onCleanup`.

10. **`src/hooks/useHotkeyRecorder.ts:175-181` — a failed hotkey save is completely silent.** `if (Result.isError(saved)) { return false; }` never calls `setError`, so if `updateHotkey`/`updateHoldToSpeakHotkey` rejects, the recorder just stays in recording mode with no feedback. Fix: `setError(...)` before returning false. (Same file line 300: `"Another hotkey is being recorded..."` and line 308 raw `watcherStarted.error.message` are shown untranslated — see #22.)

11. **`src/lib/settingsStore.ts:197-204` — `updateLanguage` is the only updater that doesn't `emit("settings-changed")`**, inconsistent with all 6 sibling updaters (lines 172-216). Fix: emit or document the exception.

12. **Locale is double-persisted with a write-only backend copy.** `src/i18n/index.ts:63-73` reads/writes `localStorage["locale"]` (the only read path — `src/index.tsx:28`), while `updateLanguage` also writes `"language"` to the Tauri store (`settingsStore.ts:130-133`); `settings().language` is never consumed anywhere (verified by grep). If localStorage is cleared, the UI reverts to English even though settings.json says otherwise. Fix: make the Tauri store the single source (read it during `initSettings` before render, or drop the store key).

13. **`src/pages/VoiceControl.tsx:291-314` — recording/transcription failures are logged and then swallowed:** on `stop_recording_failed` or `transcription_failed` the function just `return`s, the overlay hides, and the user's dictation vanishes with zero feedback. Fix: brief error state in the overlay (red bar / shake) before hiding.

14. **Every list page swallows fetch/add errors.** `src/pages/DictionaryDefault.tsx:21-24` (`if (Result.isOk(result)) setWords(...)` — else nothing) and `:36-42` (failed add: no message), `src/pages/DictionarySites.tsx:30-36`, `src/pages/DictionaryPerApp.tsx:39-42`, `src/pages/StylePerApp.tsx:32-35` and `:125` (`if (Result.isError(result)) return;`), `src/pages/StylePerSite.tsx:22-28,42`. Only TranscriptionList and ModelSettings surface errors. Fix: shared `error` signal + inline banner per page (the optimistic-update + refetch-on-error rollback pattern already there is good; it just needs a visible failure path).

15. **`src/components/TranscriptionList.tsx:100-103` — every `"transcription-created"` event resets pagination:** `fetchTranscriptions()` without cursor replaces the whole list with page 1 (line 90), discarding loaded pages and scroll position mid-scroll. Fix: prepend the new item (or fetch page 1 and merge/dedupe by id).

16. **`src/pages/DictionaryDefault.tsx:116-128` — empty state flashes before the first fetch resolves** ("NO_TERMS_FOUND" shows while `words()` is still the initial `[]`); DictionarySites/StylePerApp/StylePerSite all gate on a `loading()` signal but this page doesn't. Fix: add the same loading gate.

17. **`src/components/SettingsModal.tsx:100-171` — modal has no `role="dialog"`, no `aria-modal`, no focus trap, no focus move-in/restore**, and the `[X]` close button (line 121-127) has no `aria-label`. Fix: dialog semantics + focus management (or a `<dialog>` element).

18. **`src/components/TranscriptionCard.tsx:66-77` — the copy button only exists in the DOM while `isHovered()`**, so keyboard users can never reach it. Fix: always render it and use CSS `opacity-0 group-hover:opacity-100 focus-visible:opacity-100` (also removes the per-card mouseenter/mouseleave signal churn at lines 22,54-55).

19. **`src/components/settings/Select.tsx` (whole file) and the inline clone in `src/components/onboarding/steps/MicrophoneStep.tsx:19-84` have zero keyboard support and no listbox ARIA**; `src/components/StyleSelect.tsx` has arrow-key handling but also no `role="listbox"`/`aria-expanded`. Fix: one shared accessible Select (see #24).

20. **`src/components/AddSiteForm.tsx:53-54` — input is cleared before `await props.onAdd(...)` completes**, and since `StylePerSite.addSite` silently returns on backend error (#14), a failed add wipes the user's input with no feedback; `handleKeyDown` (line 58) also fires `handleAdd()` unawaited.
